lesson_title: The Rigged Shop, the Braai Fire and the Bank Account Under Your Feet
hook_text: Imagine a shop where your trolley buys less every year — same money, same goods. That shop is the world economy.
clip_script: Imagine a shop with rules written before you arrived: you may only sell RAW things — ore, beans, crude — and must buy back FINISHED things — phones, machines, medicine. Raw prices wobble and slide; finished prices march up. So every year your trolley of ore buys a little less. That sliding ratio has a name — the terms of trade — and it is why countries that only dig and grow stay poor while countries that MAKE get rich. The escape? Start making: turn your gold into jewellery, your chrome into steel, and climb the value chain — the ladder East Asia climbed from cheap factories to wealth. Now, what powers the climb? South Africa's economy runs on a giant braai fire: coal, four-fifths of the electricity, cheap and steady — but the smoke is warming the planet, and meanwhile we sit under the best sunshine on earth. In the Northern Cape, mirror farms around Upington focus sun into molten salt and keep generating after dark; Cape winds spin turbine forests; and through competitive bidding, that free-fuel power became cheaper than new coal. The catch: the sun clocks off, so you need batteries — including dams that pump water uphill at midnight and drop it through turbines at supper. And under it all, the real bank account: topsoil, deposited at a teaspoon a year, withdrawn by the bucket in one storm on bare ground. Sustainability is one rule: live off the interest, never the capital. Coal is capital. Sunshine is interest. Choose accordingly.
visual_style: A stylised shop with tilting price tags; a value-chain ladder from ore lump to gleaming jewellery; a night braai fire dissolving into cooling towers, then a mirror field igniting gold at dusk; water climbing a mountain into a dam and plunging back; soil draining like sand from an hourglass, then held by green contour lines.
mood: Wry and eye-opening, hardening into resolve.
pacing: Shop parable told briskly, ladder beat lands the escape, energy beats alternate warm and bright, hourglass beat slows, one-rule close hits clean.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision session and take the whole development-and-resources year in four pictures.
